questions.explanation: All three operators share the same precedence, so evaluation runs left to right: 4*8 = 32, 32%10 = 2, then 2/2 = 1. Integer division keeps the quotient, so the printed value is 1.
A macro substitutes text, not values: SQR(2 + 3) expands to 2 + 3 * 2 + 3. Multiplication binds first, so 3*2 = 6 and 2 + 6 + 3 = 11; wrapping the macro parameter in brackets would give 25.

questions.question: If a = 14 and b = -4, then what is the value of a % b?
questions.explanation: In C the sign of a % b follows the dividend, not the divisor. Since 14 = (-4)(-3) + 2, the remainder is +2 even though b is negative, so option C is correct.

Arguments are normally evaluated right to left: x>=50 uses the old 35 and gives 0, then x=50 stores 50, then x==50 gives 1, printed as 1 50 0. The standard leaves the order unspecified, which is why this question is ambiguous.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT generally used in structured programming?
questions.explanation: goto jumps to a label anywhere in the function, creating uncontrolled flow that structured programming avoids by using only sequence, selection and loops. break, continue and switch all fit structured constructs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reserved word in C?
questions.explanation: union is one of C's 32 reserved keywords and cannot be used as a name. printf is only a library function and main is the entry function, so both may legally be redefined, leaving union as the reserved word.

questions.question: What will be the default value of a global integer variable?
questions.explanation: Objects with static storage duration are zero-initialised before main() runs, and a global int belongs to that class, so it starts at 0. Only uninitialised automatic (local) variables hold garbage.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a valid C variable name?
questions.explanation: An identifier may use letters, digits and underscores and must not start with a digit. The dollar sign is not part of C's identifier character set, so int $main; is invalid while number, _rate and variable_count are fine.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to prevent any changes in the variable within a C program?
questions.explanation: const makes an object read-only after initialisation, so any later assignment is a compile-time diagnostic. immutable and mutable are not C keywords, and volatile only stops the compiler from caching a value.

questions.question: What is the sizeof(char) in a 32-bit C compiler?
questions.explanation: The C standard defines a char as exactly one byte, and sizeof reports sizes in bytes, so sizeof(char) is 1 on every 32-bit or 64-bit compiler. One byte still holds one character.
3 % -2 is 1: the quotient truncates toward zero (3/-2 = -1) and the remainder is 3 - (-2)(-1) = 1. As always in C, the sign of the remainder follows the positive dividend.
The % operator is defined only for integer operands, but here y is a float. The compiler therefore rejects y % x with a type error and no executable is produced.

options.D: Hi! followed by a garbage value

questions.explanation: Two definitions of y in the same block clash without linkage, so the compiler reports a redeclaration error and stops; the printf line is never reached. Option B would need the second line to be a plain assignment.
Multiplication and division bind tighter than addition and associate left to right: 5*9 = 45, 45/3 = 15, then 15 + 9 = 24. The division is exact, so no remainder is lost.
The conditional operator takes three expressions, but return is a statement, not an expression, so it cannot be an operand. The line is a compile-time error rather than a choice between 1 and 2.

questions.question: x = 6; y = x++; The values of x and y will be -
questions.explanation: x++ hands over the old value first and increments afterwards, so y gets 6 while x becomes 7. That matches option B (x = 7, y = 6).

questions.question: x = 6; y = ++x; The values of x and y will be -
questions.explanation: ++x increments before the value is used, so x becomes 7 and y is also assigned 7. That is the difference from post-increment and gives option D.

questions.question: The value of -17 % -5 is -
questions.explanation: -17 % -5 is -2 because -17 = (-5)(3) + (-2), and the remainder takes the sign of the dividend. Neither 2 nor -3 satisfies that identity, so B is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a valid C variable name?
questions.explanation: Identifiers may contain only letters, digits and underscores. The $ character is illegal in C, so int $main; is the invalid declaration while number, rate and variable_count are all valid.

questions.question: All keywords in C are in -
questions.explanation: C is case-sensitive and every keyword is spelled in lowercase, for example int, while, return and sizeof. Writing Int or WHILE creates a different identifier, not a keyword.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be a variable name in C?
questions.explanation: volatile is a type qualifier keyword and can never name a variable. true is not a standard C keyword (C99 supplies it as a macro in stdbool.h), and friend and export are not C keywords either.

questions.question: The C-preprocessors are specified with symbol -
questions.explanation: Every preprocessor directive begins with #, as in #include, #define and #ifdef. The dollar, double-quote and ampersand symbols have no preprocessor meaning at the start of a line.

questions.question: In C compiler there are -
questions.explanation: ANSI C (C89) defines exactly 32 keywords, including int, if, else, while, struct, union and sizeof. Later standards add a few more, but 32 is the classical answer for this paper.

questions.question: && is a/an ________ operator.
questions.explanation: && is the logical AND: it yields 1 only when both operands are non-zero and short-circuits otherwise. A single & would be the bitwise AND, so neither arithmetic nor unary fits.
a++ returns the current value and then increments, so b becomes 5 while a becomes 6. printf lists a first, so the output is 6 5 (option A).

questions.question: If x = -5 and y = 3 then the value of x % y is -
questions.explanation: The remainder takes the sign of the dividend: -5 = 3(-1) + (-2), so -5 % 3 is -2. Option 2 would be the answer only if the remainder followed the divisor.

questions.question: Who is the father of C language?
questions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Laboratories around 1972 to build UNIX. James Gosling created Java and Rasmus Lerdorf created PHP, so option C is the father of C.
Multiplication and division are evaluated before addition: 4/2 = 2 and 6*2 = 12, so 2 + 2 + 12 = 16. Strict left-to-right reading would wrongly give 15.

questions.question: 'C' is often called a -
questions.explanation: C is a high-level language because its statements are written for humans and translated by a compiler. It also offers low-level facilities such as pointers, which is why it is sometimes called middle-level.

questions.question: Which operator has the lowest priority?
questions.explanation: Logical OR (||) has the lowest precedence of the four: ++ binds tightest, then %, then +, and || is evaluated last. So the overall value is decided by ||.

questions.question: Which escape character can be used to begin a new line in C?
questions.explanation: \n is the newline escape that moves the cursor to the start of the next line. \a rings the bell, \b moves back one character, and \m is not a defined escape sequence.

questions.question: The value of -17 % -5 is -
questions.explanation: -17 % -5 leaves -2, because -17 = (-5)(3) + (-2) and the sign follows the dividend. Since -2 is not among 3.4, 3 or -3, the answer is none of these.

questions.question: x = 5; y = x++; The values of x and y will be -
questions.explanation: Post-increment supplies the old value and then increments, so y = 5 and x becomes 6, which is option B (y = 5, x = 6). Option A would need ++x instead.

questions.question: Which is valid C expression?
questions.explanation: A single integer literal cannot contain a comma, so 100,000 becomes three tokens, and $ is not allowed in identifiers. Only int my_num = 100000; is a valid C declaration.
SQUARE(n) expands to n*n without brackets, so 64 / 4 * 4 is evaluated left to right: 64/4 = 16 and 16*4 = 64. Bracketing the macro expansion would give 4 instead.
Assignment associates right to left, so y = x = 10 stores 10 in x and then in y. z = x < 10 tests whether 10 < 10, which is false (0), giving x=10 y=10 z=0.
num is 30, so num > 5 is true and the inner conditional runs. 30 <= 10 is false, so the inner expression yields 200 and the outer 500 branch is never taken.
The declared return type is int, so the computed value is converted to int before being returned; the (double) and (char) casts only affect intermediate values. Hence the function returns int.

Which of the following is a valid variable name in C?
questions.explanation: roll_no mixes letters with an underscore, which is a legal identifier. & is the address-of operator, a space splits the name into two tokens, and the hyphen would be read as subtraction.

questions.question: What is the difference between including a header file with < > and " " in C?

options.A: No difference; both work the same
options.B: < > searches standard library directories; " " searches current directory first
options.C: " " searches standard library; < > searches current directory
options.D: < > is for C++ only; " " is for C

questions.explanation: Angle brackets send the compiler to the implementation's standard include directories, while double quotes search the source file's own directory first and then fall back to those standard paths.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the C language?

options.D: C allows direct memory manipulation using pointers

questions.explanation: C is procedural and structured; classes, inheritance and polymorphism came with C++. Portability, structured constructs and direct memory access through pointers are all real C features.

questions.question: The scanf() function is declared in which header file?
questions.explanation: scanf() and printf() are both declared in stdio.h, the standard input/output header. conio.h is a non-standard compiler header, stdlib.h holds utilities and string.h holds string functions.

questions.question: Long int variable in a 32-bit C compiler occupies how many bytes in main memory?
questions.explanation: On a 32-bit compiler a long int is 4 bytes (32 bits), the same width as int there. The standard only guarantees at least 4 bytes, which is why 8 bytes appears on some 64-bit systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of structured programming?

options.B: Code is reusable and easy to maintain

questions.explanation: Structured programmes are built from functions with single entry and exit points, which makes code reusable, testable and easier to maintain. They avoid goto and are not automatically slower.

questions.question: What is the result of the expression 5 & 3 in C?
questions.explanation: 5 is 0101 and 3 is 0011 in binary; bitwise AND keeps only bits set in both, giving 0001 = 1. OR (|) would give 7 and XOR (^) would give 6.

questions.question: What does the sizeof operator return in C?

options.A: The value stored in a variable
options.B: The memory address of a variable
options.C: The size in bytes of a data type or variable
options.D: The number of elements in an array

questions.explanation: sizeof is a compile-time unary operator that reports the storage size of a type or expression in bytes, so sizeof(int) is 2 or 4 depending on the compiler. It does not read the stored value.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of constant in C?
questions.explanation: Classical C has integer, floating-point, character and string constants but no boolean constant type; true and false arrive only as stdbool.h macros in C99. So 'boolean constant' is not a C constant type.
